label: prop:em-coupling-bring-zero-mode
title: Additive Bring zero-mode form $1/\alpha_{EM} = q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q + 2g/(4\pi(g-1))$ (conditional)
html:
Conditional on the additive self-consistency postulate and the [10]_q tree coefficient. Let g = 4 denote the genus of Bring's surface. This is the unique Riemann surface supporting the genus-4 torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} (force-carrier uniqueness). Assume that the zero-mode density of Bring's surface enters 1/\alpha_{EM} additively alongside the tree term, and that the tree coefficient of T_{3,5} is [10]_q. Then

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{EM}}
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q}_{\text{tree level}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\frac{2g}{4\pi(g-1)}}_{\text{Bring zero-mode}}
  \;+\;
  \mathcal{O}(\alpha)
  \;=\;
  q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q + \frac{2}{3\pi} + \mathcal{O}(\alpha).

The constant 2/(3\pi) = 8/(12\pi) admits two independent geometric identifications on Bring's surface:

  1. Hodge / Gauss-Bonnet ratio: 
    \frac{2g}{4\pi(g-1)} \;=\; \frac{\dim H^1(M_{\text{Bring}};\,\mathbb{R})}{\mathrm{Area}(M_{\text{Bring}})}.
    The area evaluates under constant negative curvature -1 as \mathrm{Area} = -2\pi\chi = 4\pi(g-1) = 12\pi.
  2. Sphere-volume ratio: 
    \frac{2}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^2)}{3\cdot\mathrm{Vol}(S^3)} \;=\; \frac{4\pi}{3\cdot 2\pi^2}.

Numerical match

Evaluation at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps) using 60 dps precision yields:

Quantity Value
q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q 136.823219729\ldots
2/(3\pi) = 2g/(4\pi(g-1)) 0.212206591\ldots
Sum 137.035426320\ldots
CODATA-2022 1/\alpha 137.035999177(21)
Residual (relative) -4.2 \times 10^{-6}

The second additive term \alpha/(4\pi) \approx 5.81 \times 10^{-4} brings the relative residual to +5.7 \times 10^{-8}. This approaches the CODATA standard deviation \sigma_\alpha \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-10}.

Conjectural physical interpretation

The numerical match supports a structural decomposition:

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{EM}}
  \;=\;
  q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q
  \;+\;
  \frac{2g}{4\pi(g-1)}
  \;+\;
  \mathcal{O}(\alpha).

The g = 4 structure of Bring's surface appears in both main terms. The tree-level coefficient [9]_q[10]_q derives from the unique pair of genus-4 torus knots \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\} (force-carrier uniqueness). The infrared shift 2g/(4\pi(g-1)) emerges from the Hodge data of the same Bring's surface. This double appearance of g = 4 is structurally consistent. It matches the expectations for a categorical-Lagrangian quantum field theory with a UV completion on Bring's curve.

Conditional theorem. The constant 2/(3\pi) = b_1/\mathrm{Area} is proved at g = 4 without further hypotheses. What is assumed is the following. (i) The additive postulate itself: that the zero-mode density is added to 1/\alpha_{EM}. (ii) The [10]_q tree coefficient of T_{3,5}, which holds only for one choice of character weights. (iii) The normalisation [2]_q/(8\pi) of the one-loop term. (iv) The coefficient c of the next-order term \alpha\,[2]_q/(8\pi)\,(1 - c\,h^2\alpha), h = q - q^{-1}. The archimedean dilogarithm limit holds on [0,1), which covers every argument used here. Bloch-Suslin pentagon uniqueness holds only for the zero functor on the reals and carries no content. A Bloch-group class realising 2/(3\pi) is not needed. At q = 1 the additive form keeps 2/(3\pi) + \alpha/(4\pi), while the Chern-Simons correction form reduces to the tree term. Neither is a truncation of the other.

Form Type Residual at q_0 Structural status
Bare q[9]_q[10]_q multiplicative tree -1.55\times 10^{-3} Derived
Conjectured Chern-Simons correction form multiplicative + Gram-det \kappa -4\times 10^{-7} \kappa unproved
This conjecture (additive Bring zero-mode) q[9]_q[10]_q + 2g/(4\pi(g-1)) -4.2\times 10^{-6} Geometrically clean; one Bring-genus-4 quantity in each term

The additive form provides the cleanest structure. It avoids fitted coefficients. Every factor maps to a known geometric or topological invariant of Bring's surface.
